The clinical presentation of a finger resting in extension with an inability to flex the DIP joint after a hyperextension injury is classic for a flexor digitorum profundus rupture, known as Jersey Finger. The negative X-ray rules out fracture, and the normal ultrasound may be a false negative or limited in visualizing the retracted tendon. Given the specific mechanism and physical exam findings, I am confident in the diagnosis.
